open_questions: RUWE 2.347 hints at binarity but Gaia extra fields flag low; RV and Gaia N/A do not test

Sector depths vary by source (SPOC 2-min 17742 ppm vs TESS-SPOC 12962 ppm, verdict differs_by_source) but stay consistent within each source, leaving a flat-bottom look (shape v_sigma -3.967) with a stellar variability explanation
dossier.public_summary: A 1.5% dip repeats every 0.528 days but the star itself brightens and dims by ~3% at that same period and shows a strong phase curve. The dip lines up with the star's rotation and with its brightness changes, not with a planet transit. It is best explained by stellar variability / close binarity, not a 7.7-Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Duration ratio 1.591 is longer than expected and xgboost planet_rank 0.11 rates it planet-unlike; together with variability this favours a close binary/spot signal over a planet.
